components.note: 豆 — an old stemmed serving dish, later borrowed for beans; in 豆腐 tofu, 土豆 potato.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 奶奶在花园里种了很多豆子。
example.pinyin: Nǎinai zài huāyuán lǐ zhòng le hěn duō dòuzi.
example.english: Grandma planted a lot of beans in the garden.
example.fact: Bean plants, like other legumes, host colonies of Rhizobium bacteria in nodules on their roots that convert atmospheric nitrogen into a form plants can use, a process called nitrogen fixation. Farmers have exploited this for millennia by rotating legume crops with cereals, naturally replenishing soil fertility without synthetic fertilizer.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈每天早上用豆子磨豆浆。
examples.pinyin: Māma měitiān zǎoshang yòng dòuzi mó dòujiāng.
examples.english: Mom grinds beans to make soy milk every morning.

examples.hanzi: 他在锅里炒了一把豆子。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài guō lǐ chǎo le yī bǎ dòuzi.
examples.english: He stir-fried a handful of beans in the pan.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 撒 is scattering or letting go.
散 (sàn) scatter is the meaning-sound part: a hand 扌 scattering, with sā/sàn close in sound.
尸 (body, a crouching figure) — also in 屁 and 屎; 尿 is body plus 水 (water).
水 (water) — liquid passed from the body.

example.hanzi: 小狗到处撒尿来标记自己的地盘。
example.pinyin: Xiǎogǒu dàochù sāniào lái biāojì zìjǐ de dìpán.
example.english: The puppy urinates everywhere to mark its territory.
example.fact: Many mammals, including dogs and wolves, use urine to mark territory because it carries pheromones and other chemical signals that convey information about an individual's identity, sex, and reproductive status to other animals. Wolves in a pack will often mark boundaries with urine at regular intervals along well-traveled trails, effectively posting chemical 'signs' that discourage rival packs from intruding.

examples.hanzi: 小孩子在路边撒尿，妈妈赶紧带他去厕所。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo háizi zài lùbiān sāniào, māma gǎnjǐn dài tā qù cèsuǒ.
examples.english: The little boy was peeing by the road, so his mom rushed him to the toilet.

examples.hanzi: 小狗每次出门都要撒尿。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎogǒu měi cì chūmén dōu yào sāniào.
examples.english: The puppy pees every time it goes out.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — a person with swinging arms above a foot 止. As a radical it marks movement: 起, 越, 超, 趣.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 老板生气地让他马上走人。
example.pinyin: Lǎobǎn shēngqì de ràng tā mǎshàng zǒurén.
example.english: The boss angrily told him to leave immediately.
example.fact: The phrase 'quiet quitting' went viral in 2022 to describe employees who do only the minimum required by their job description, though the underlying behavior — psychologists call it 'work disengagement' — has been studied by organizational researchers since at least the 1990s. Gallup's long-running workplace surveys have consistently found that only around a third of employees globally report feeling genuinely engaged at work.

examples.hanzi: 你要是不满意，大可以走人。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yàoshi bù mǎnyì, dà kěyǐ zǒurén.
examples.english: If you're not satisfied, you can just leave.

examples.hanzi: 活干完了，我们就走人。
examples.pinyin: Huó gàn wán le, wǒmen jiù zǒurén.
examples.english: Once the job is done, we'll be off.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — the vertical stroke 丨 is the string being drawn back on a bow — 引 is to pull, then to attract and to cite.
用 (use) — early picture is debated: a pail, a fenced enclosure or a hung bell. Memory aid: a door-frame 冂 with a cross-bar — a tool 'put to use' (使用, 不用).

example.hanzi: 这篇论文引用了很多权威资料。
example.pinyin: Zhè piān lùnwén yǐnyòng le hěn duō quánwēi zīliào.
example.english: This paper cites a lot of authoritative sources.
example.fact: In 2005, physicist Jorge Hirsch introduced the h-index, a single number meant to capture both the productivity and citation impact of a researcher's published work. Despite well-documented flaws — it ignores field-specific citation norms and rewards long careers over recent quality — the h-index remains one of the most widely used metrics in academic hiring and promotion decisions.

examples.hanzi: 这篇文章引用了一句古诗。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān wénzhāng yǐnyòng le yī jù gǔshī.
examples.english: This article quotes a line of classical poetry.

examples.hanzi: 引用别人的话要注明出处。
examples.pinyin: Yǐnyòng biéren de huà yào zhùmíng chūchù.
examples.english: When quoting someone's words, you should cite the source.

components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings: 情 emotion, 快 happy, 怕 afraid; 怜 is feeling pity.
令 (lìng) is a loose sound hint (lián/líng); same part in 铃 líng and 零 líng.
忄 (heart) — pity in the heart; also in 怜 pity, 情 feeling.
闵 (mǐn) gives the exact sound.

example.hanzi: 她对流浪的动物充满了怜悯之心。
example.pinyin: Tā duì liúlàng de dòngwù chōngmǎn le liánmǐn zhī xīn.
example.english: She is full of pity for stray animals.
example.fact: In the early 1990s, neuroscientists in Parma, Italy, led by Giacomo Rizzolatti, discovered 'mirror neurons' in macaque monkeys — brain cells that fire both when an animal performs an action and when it merely observes another individual performing that same action. The finding sparked decades of research into whether a similar mechanism in humans underlies empathy and our capacity to feel compassion for others' suffering.

examples.hanzi: 他对那个可怜的孩子产生了怜悯。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì nàge kělián de háizi chǎnshēng le liánmǐn.
examples.english: He felt pity for that poor child.

examples.hanzi: 法官出于怜悯，减轻了他的刑罚。
examples.pinyin: Fǎguān chūyú liánmǐn, jiǎnqīng le tā de xíngfá.
examples.english: Out of mercy, the judge reduced his sentence.

components.note: 才 (talent, just) — a sprout pushing out of the ground. 才 also sounds out 材 cái and 财 cái.
能 (can) — originally a picture of a bear, a strong animal (熊 xióng adds fire 灬); "strong, able" gave "can".

example.hanzi: 每个孩子都有自己独特的才能。
example.pinyin: Měi gè háizi dōu yǒu zìjǐ dútè de cáinéng.
example.english: Every child has their own unique talents.
example.fact: The idea that mastering a skill requires roughly 10,000 hours of practice was popularized by journalist Malcolm Gladwell in his 2008 book 'Outliers,' drawing on research by psychologist Anders Ericsson into expert violinists. Ericsson himself later pushed back on the oversimplified rule, emphasizing that the quality of practice — specifically, deliberate practice with focused feedback — matters far more than raw hours logged.

examples.hanzi: 他在音乐方面很有才能。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yīnyuè fāngmiàn hěn yǒu cáinéng.
examples.english: He has great talent in music.

examples.hanzi: 公司需要能发挥你才能的岗位。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī xūyào néng fāhuī nǐ cáinéng de gǎngwèi.
examples.english: The company needs a position where your abilities can shine.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person and his word: 言 (speech) beside it gives a person who keeps his word, hence "trust, believe".
言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters, as in 说, 请, 谢.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位.
牛 (ox) — in the traditional reading, a person 亻 dividing up an ox: one piece, hence 件 as a measure word for items.

example.hanzi: 邮递员每天早上送来大量的信件。
example.pinyin: Yóudìyuán měitiān zǎoshang sòng lái dàliàng de xìnjiàn.
example.english: The postman delivers a large amount of mail every morning.
example.fact: The Penny Black, issued in Britain in May 1840, was the world's first adhesive postage stamp, and its introduction let senders prepay postage rather than making recipients pay on delivery. The reform, championed by Rowland Hill, was credited with dramatically increasing mail volume across Britain within just a few years.

examples.hanzi: 我每个星期都会收到几封信件。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi gè xīngqī dōu huì shōudào jǐ fēng xìnjiàn.
examples.english: I receive several letters every week.

examples.hanzi: 请把这些信件放进邮箱里。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhèxiē xìnjiàn fàng jìn yóuxiāng lǐ.
examples.english: Please put these letters in the mailbox.

components.note: 电 (electric) — simplified from 電: 雨 rain over 申, a lightning bolt (申 originally pictured a flash).
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 给, 组; 线 is thread or line.
戋 (jiān) is a loose sound clue; same part in 浅 qiǎn, 钱 qián and 残 cán.

example.hanzi: 施工队正在检查地下的电线。
example.pinyin: Shīgōngduì zhèngzài jiǎnchá dìxià de diànxiàn.
example.english: The construction crew is inspecting the underground electric wires.
example.fact: In the late 1880s, Thomas Edison and George Westinghouse fought the so-called 'War of Currents' over whether homes should be wired for direct current (DC), which Edison championed, or alternating current (AC), backed by Westinghouse and Nikola Tesla. AC eventually won out because it could be transmitted efficiently over much longer distances at high voltage, and it remains the standard for power grids worldwide today.

examples.hanzi: 小猫咬坏了桌子下面的电线。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎomāo yǎo huài le zhuōzi xiàmiàn de diànxiàn.
examples.english: The kitten chewed the wire under the table.

examples.hanzi: 大风把路边的电线吹断了。
examples.pinyin: Dàfēng bǎ lùbiān de diànxiàn chuī duàn le.
examples.english: The strong wind blew down the power lines by the road.

components.note: 日 (sun) — exposure to the sun; also in 晒 dry in the sun, 晴 sunny.
暴 (bào) gives the sound; it also sounds out 瀑 pù and 爆 bào.
火 (fire) — fire above a person (儿 legs) — a person carrying fire gives light; 光 is bright and shining, as in 阳光, 时光.
儿 (legs, person) — the bottom 儿 is a walking person, seen also in 先, 兄, 元.

example.hanzi: 这张照片曝光过度，看起来太亮了。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhàopiàn bàoguāng guòdù, kàn qǐlái tài liàng le.
example.english: This photo is overexposed and looks too bright.
example.fact: The oldest surviving photograph made in a camera, taken by French inventor Nicéphore Niépce around 1826–27, required an exposure time of roughly eight hours, during which the sun visibly moved across the sky and lit both sides of the courtyard in the image. Modern digital cameras can achieve a comparable exposure in a fraction of a millisecond.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司的丑闻被媒体曝光了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī de chǒuwén bèi méitǐ bàoguāng le.
examples.english: This company's scandal was exposed by the media.

examples.hanzi: 拍夜景时，曝光时间要长一点。
examples.pinyin: Pāi yèjǐng shí, bàoguāng shíjiān yào cháng yīdiǎn.
examples.english: When shooting night scenes, the exposure time should be longer.

components.note: 彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.
禾 (grain) — grain radical — 程 first meant to measure grain, hence standard, then course and journey; also in 种, 秋, 稿.
呈 (chéng) — same sound — 程 is chéng; 呈 also sounds out 逞 chěng.

example.hanzi: 这次旅行的行程安排得非常紧凑。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì lǚxíng de xíngchéng ānpái de fēicháng jǐncòu.
example.english: The itinerary for this trip is scheduled very tightly.
example.fact: Marco Polo's journey from Venice to the court of Kublai Khan, recounted in 'The Travels of Marco Polo,' took roughly four years to complete via the Silk Road, covering thousands of kilometers by camel caravan, horse, and boat. His account, written after he returned to Europe in 1295, became one of the most influential travel narratives in shaping European curiosity about Asia.

examples.hanzi: 我们的行程已经安排好了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de xíngchéng yǐjīng ānpái hǎo le.
examples.english: Our itinerary has already been arranged.

examples.hanzi: 因为大雪，他取消了明天的行程。
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi dàxuě, tā qǔxiāo le míngtiān de xíngchéng.
examples.english: Because of heavy snow, he canceled tomorrow's trip.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hitting; also in 打 hit, 推 push.
童 (tóng) is only a loose sound clue for zhuàng.
凵 (open box) — the bottom part and dictionary radical. 击 simplifies 擊, whose 手 (hand) hinted at striking. Memory aid: a blow landing in a hollow.

example.hanzi: 两辆车在十字路口发生了撞击。
example.pinyin: Liǎng liàng chē zài shízìlùkǒu fāshēng le zhuàngjī.
example.english: The two cars collided at the intersection.
example.fact: The Chicxulub impact, a roughly 10-kilometer-wide asteroid that struck what is now Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula about 66 million years ago, released energy equivalent to billions of atomic bombs and is widely believed to have triggered the mass extinction that wiped out most dinosaurs. The crater it left behind, over 150 kilometers across, was only confirmed via geological and gravitational surveys in the 1990s.

examples.hanzi: 陨石撞击地面，留下了一个大坑。
examples.pinyin: Yǔnshí zhuàngjī dìmiàn, liúxià le yī gè dà kēng.
examples.english: The meteorite struck the ground and left a big crater.

examples.hanzi: 海浪不停地撞击着岩石。
examples.pinyin: Hǎilàng bù tíng de zhuàngjī zhe yánshí.
examples.english: The waves keep crashing against the rocks.

components.note: 也 (also) — began as a picture (a vessel or snake; scholars disagree) and was borrowed for 'also'. A loose sound clue in 他 tā, 她 tā, 地 dì, 池 chí.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.

example.hanzi: 你不想去也好，我们可以下次再约。
example.pinyin: Nǐ bùxiǎng qù yěhǎo, wǒmen kěyǐ xiàcì zài yuē.
example.english: It's fine if you don't want to go; we can plan for another time.
example.fact: The 1978 Camp David Accords, brokered by U.S. President Jimmy Carter between Israel and Egypt, took 12 days of intense negotiation at the presidential retreat to produce a framework for peace, ending decades of conflict between the two nations. It remains one of the most significant diplomatic agreements in modern Middle Eastern history.

examples.hanzi: 你去也好，不去也好，都没关系。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ qù yě hǎo, bù qù yě hǎo, dōu méi guānxi.
examples.english: Whether you go or not, it doesn't matter.

examples.hanzi: 没有也好，省得我们花钱。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu yě hǎo, shěngde wǒmen huā qián.
examples.english: It's fine if there isn't one, which saves us money.

components.note: 木 (tree) — a tree with a mark at the base: the root, hence source, origin, and the measure word for books.
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 情, 快, 怕; 性 is the inner nature of a thing.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint; also in 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 善良是他的本性。
example.pinyin: Shànliáng shì tā de běnxìng.
example.english: Kindness is his true nature.
example.fact: The Minnesota Study of Twins Reared Apart, launched in 1979 by psychologist Thomas Bouchard, tracked identical twins separated at birth and raised in different families, finding striking similarities in personality, IQ, and even specific habits despite years apart. The research became a landmark case for the influence of genetics — an inborn 'nature' — on human behavior, though scientists agree environment still plays a substantial role.

examples.hanzi: 江山易改，本性难移。
examples.pinyin: Jiāngshān yì gǎi, běnxìng nán yí.
examples.english: Rivers and mountains may change, but one's nature is hard to change.

examples.hanzi: 小孩好动是他们的本性。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎohái hàodòng shì tāmen de běnxìng.
examples.english: Being active is a child's natural instinct.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hitting or throwing oneself; also in 打 hit, 推 push.
卜 (bǔ) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 朴 pǔ and 仆 pú.

example.hanzi: 小狗向我扑过来。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu xiàng wǒ pū guòlái.
example.english: The puppy pounced at me.
example.fact: 扑 includes 扑克 (poker), 扑灭 (to put out) and 扑面而来 ('to rush at your face'). 扑通 is the sound of a splash.

examples.hanzi: 孩子高兴地扑到妈妈怀里。
examples.pinyin: Háizi gāoxìng de pū dào māma huái lǐ.
examples.english: The child happily threw himself into his mother's arms.

examples.hanzi: 一阵香味扑鼻而来。
examples.pinyin: Yí zhèn xiāngwèi pūbí ér lái.
examples.english: A waft of fragrance hit my nose.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — marks weather and moisture, as in 雪, 雷, 雾; 露 is dew.
路 (lù) gives the sound exactly: 露 lù (dew) or lòu (reveal).
营 (yíng) — camp, to run a business; as a part it sounds out 荧 yíng, 萤 yíng and 莹 yíng.

example.hanzi: 这个周末我们打算去山里露营。
example.pinyin: Zhè gè zhōumò wǒmen dǎsuàn qù shān lǐ lùyíng.
example.english: This weekend we plan to go camping in the mountains.
example.fact: Yellowstone, established in 1872, was the world's first national park, created specifically to protect its geothermal features — including the geyser Old Faithful — from private development. Its creation inspired the modern national park movement, which now protects wilderness areas, many of them popular camping destinations, in more than 100 countries.

examples.hanzi: 我们昨晚在湖边露营。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zuówǎn zài húbiān lùyíng.
examples.english: We camped by the lake last night.

examples.hanzi: 露营时要注意防火。
examples.pinyin: Lùyíng shí yào zhùyì fánghuǒ.
examples.english: Be careful about fire when camping.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — plants; 草 is grass itself, as in 花 flower, 菜 vegetable.
早 (zǎo) shares the rhyme -ǎo with cǎo, a loose sound clue.
土 (earth) — flat ground; also in 地 ground, 城 city.
平 (píng) gives the exact sound and the idea of flat; it also sounds out 评 píng and 苹 píng.

example.hanzi: 孩子们在草坪上玩得很开心。
example.pinyin: Háizimen zài cǎopíng shàng wán de hěn kāixīn.
example.english: The children had a great time playing on the lawn.
example.fact: The modern lawnmower was invented in 1830 by English engineer Edwin Beard Budding, who adapted a rotary blade mechanism used to trim the nap off woolen cloth in textile mills. Before his invention, maintaining a lawn required scything by hand or grazing livestock, which meant manicured grass lawns were largely a luxury reserved for the wealthy.

examples.hanzi: 请不要踩草坪。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bù yào cǎi cǎopíng.
examples.english: Please don't walk on the lawn.

examples.hanzi: 爸爸周末在院子里修剪草坪。
examples.pinyin: Bàba zhōumò zài yuànzi lǐ xiūjiǎn cǎopíng.
examples.english: Dad mows the lawn in the yard on weekends.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — words passed down through ten 十 generations of mouths — old; 古 also sounds out 姑 gū and 故 gù.
艹 (grass) — plants; also in 花 flower, 草 grass.
重 (zhòng) is only a loose clue; 懂 dǒng (to understand) shares 董 and sounds the same.

example.hanzi: 他收藏了很多明清时期的古董。
example.pinyin: Tā shōucáng le hěn duō Míng Qīng shíqī de gǔdǒng.
example.english: He collects many antiques from the Ming and Qing dynasties.
example.fact: Ming dynasty (1368–1644) blue-and-white porcelain was so prized across Asia, the Middle East, and Europe that it inspired imitation industries in Persia and the Netherlands (Delftware), centuries before global trade was common. Genuine pieces routinely sell at auction today for millions of dollars, and experts still rely on details like glaze crackling and cobalt pigment composition to distinguish authentic antiques from later reproductions.

examples.hanzi: 这件古董花瓶价值连城。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn gǔdǒng huāpíng jiàzhí liánchéng.
examples.english: This antique vase is priceless.

examples.hanzi: 他喜欢逛古董市场，淘便宜货。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan guàng gǔdǒng shìchǎng, táo piányi huò.
examples.english: He likes strolling through antique markets to hunt for bargains.

components.note: 各 (each) — a foot 夂 arriving at a place 口: each one coming. 各 also sounds out 路 lù, 格 gé, 客 kè and 洛 luò.
人 (person) — the top part. 个 is the general measure word, as in 一个, 这个, 那个.
丨 (a vertical tally) — under 人, read as one tally mark per person: counting individuals one by one.

example.hanzi: 这个问题涉及社会的各个方面。
example.pinyin: Zhè gè wèntí shèjí shèhuì de gègè fāngmiàn.
example.english: This issue involves every aspect of society.
example.fact: In a honeybee colony, individual workers specialize in different roles — nursing larvae, foraging, guarding the hive, or cleaning — and can shift between these jobs as they age or as the colony's needs change, a division of labor biologists call 'polyethism.' Coordinating each of these separate roles without any central planner is what lets a colony of tens of thousands function as a single, resilient unit.

examples.hanzi: 会议的各个环节都安排得很好。
examples.pinyin: Huìyì de gègè huánjié dōu ānpái de hěn hǎo.
examples.english: Every part of the meeting was well arranged.

examples.hanzi: 警察把嫌疑人各个击破。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá bǎ xiányírén gègè jī pò.
examples.english: The police broke the suspects down one by one.

components.note: 面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.
木 (wood, tree) — 条 was a long slender twig, so branch, strip, and then the measure word for long things; 木 as in 树, 板.

example.hanzi: 妈妈煮了一碗热腾腾的面条。
example.pinyin: Māma zhǔ le yì wǎn rèténgténg de miàntiáo.
example.english: Mom cooked a steaming bowl of noodles.
example.fact: In 2005, archaeologists excavating the Lajia site in northwestern China's Qinghai province discovered a bowl containing the remains of noodles made from foxtail and broomcorn millet, dated to roughly 4,000 years ago. The find pushed back the earliest known evidence of noodle-making by about 2,000 years and settled part of a long debate over whether noodles originated in China or the Middle East.

examples.hanzi: 我晚饭想吃一碗牛肉面条。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ wǎnfàn xiǎng chī yī wǎn niúròu miàntiáo.
examples.english: I want a bowl of beef noodles for dinner.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的手工面条特别有嚼劲。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de shǒugōng miàntiáo tèbié yǒu jiáojìn.
examples.english: The handmade noodles at this shop are especially chewy.

components.note: 田 (field) — 画 (simplified 畫) originally showed a brush 聿 drawing the borders of a field: to draw lines, hence a picture.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.

example.hanzi: 这位画家的作品在世界各地展出。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi huàjiā de zuòpǐn zài shìjiè gèdì zhǎnchū.
example.english: This painter's works are exhibited all over the world.
example.fact: Dutch painter Vincent van Gogh created more than 2,000 artworks in just over a decade but is believed to have sold only a single painting, 'The Red Vineyard,' during his lifetime. Today his works, including 'The Starry Night' and 'Sunflowers,' are among the most valuable and recognizable paintings in the world, with some selling at auction for over $80 million.

examples.hanzi: 他从小就想成为一名画家。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù xiǎng chéngwéi yī míng huàjiā.
examples.english: He has wanted to be a painter since childhood.

examples.hanzi: 这位画家喜欢画山水和花鸟。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi huàjiā xǐhuan huà shānshuǐ hé huāniǎo.
examples.english: This painter likes to paint landscapes, flowers and birds.

components.note: 纟 (silk, simplified 糸) — plain unmixed thread, hence pure; also in 红 red, 级 level.
屯 (tún) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 钝 dùn and 顿 dùn.
氵 (water) — washing clean; also in 洗 wash, 清 clear.
吉 (jí) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 结 jié.

example.hanzi: 孩子的心灵总是那么纯洁。
example.pinyin: Háizi de xīnlíng zǒngshì nàme chúnjié.
example.english: A child's heart is always so pure.
example.fact: Ultrapure water used in semiconductor manufacturing must have virtually every dissolved mineral, ion, and particle removed — far cleaner than drinking water — because even microscopic contaminants can ruin the nanometer-scale circuits etched onto a silicon wafer. Producing it requires a multi-stage process of reverse osmosis, deionization, and ultrafiltration that can take a facility days to fully purify a single batch.

examples.hanzi: 她有一颗纯洁善良的心。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu yī kē chúnjié shànliáng de xīn.
examples.english: She has a pure and kind heart.

examples.hanzi: 雪后的世界看起来那么纯洁。
examples.pinyin: Xuě hòu de shìjiè kàn qǐlái nàme chúnjié.
examples.english: The world after snowfall looks so pure.

components.note: 阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — hills and places: 院, 阳, 陆; 陪 is to sit by one's side.
咅 (pōu) is a loose sound clue; same part in 培 péi, 赔 péi, 倍 bèi.
亻 (person) — person radical — 伴 is a companion, as in 伙伴.
半 (bàn) — same sound — 伴 is bàn, like 半; 半 also sounds out 拌 bàn and 叛 pàn.

example.hanzi: 狗是人类忠实的陪伴动物。
example.pinyin: Gǒu shì rénlèi zhōngshí de péibàn dòngwù.
example.english: Dogs are loyal companion animals for humans.
example.fact: Genetic studies suggest dogs were domesticated from wolves somewhere between 15,000 and 40,000 years ago, making them the oldest domesticated animal species and predating agriculture by thousands of years. Some researchers argue the relationship began when wolves that tolerated human camps and scavenged food scraps gradually evolved into companions, long before any deliberate breeding took place.

examples.hanzi: 谢谢你一直陪伴在我身边。
examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ yīzhí péibàn zài wǒ shēnbiān.
examples.english: Thank you for always being by my side.

examples.hanzi: 孩子的成长需要父母的陪伴。
examples.pinyin: Háizi de chéngzhǎng xūyào fùmǔ de péibàn.
examples.english: A child's growth needs parents' company.

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
阝 (hill, from 阜) — marks slopes and boundaries, as in 院, 陆, 阶; 限 is a limit.
艮 (gèn) is only a loose hint for xiàn; 根 gēn and 跟 gēn share it.

example.hanzi: 宇宙的边界似乎是无限的。
example.pinyin: Yǔzhòu de biānjiè sìhū shì wúxiàn de.
example.english: The boundary of the universe seems to be unlimited.
example.fact: Cosmologists distinguish between the 'observable universe,' which has a finite radius of about 46 billion light-years because light from farther away hasn't had time to reach us since the Big Bang, and the universe as a whole, whose total extent is unknown and could in fact be infinite. This distinction means that even an infinite universe could appear to have a boundary simply because of the finite speed of light.

examples.hanzi: 这个孩子的想象力是无限的。
examples.pinyin: Zhège háizi de xiǎngxiànglì shì wúxiàn de.
examples.english: This child's imagination is limitless.

examples.hanzi: 生命虽然短暂，但意义是无限的。
examples.pinyin: Shēngmìng suīrán duǎnzàn, dàn yìyì shì wúxiàn de.
examples.english: Life is brief, but its meaning is boundless.

components.note: 田 (field) — a field above 力 (strength): a man is one who works the fields with strength.
子 (child) — children and offspring, as in 孙 grandchild, 学 study, 字 character; 孩 is a young child.
亥 (hài) is a close sound clue for hái; 亥 also sounds out 该 gāi, 核 hé and 刻 kè.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 那个男孩子在公园里踢足球。
example.pinyin: Nà gè nánháizi zài gōngyuán lǐ tī zúqiú.
example.english: That boy is playing soccer in the park.
example.fact: Modern association football's first standardized rules were drawn up in 1863 in London when representatives of several English football clubs met to form the Football Association, settling long-running disputes over whether players could carry the ball with their hands. Clubs that insisted on keeping the handling rule split off to form rugby football instead.

examples.hanzi: 男孩子也可以哭，这没什么丢人的。
examples.pinyin: Nán háizi yě kěyǐ kū, zhè méi shénme diūrén de.
examples.english: Boys can cry too, and there's nothing shameful about it.

examples.hanzi: 我家有两个男孩子，吵得不得了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu liǎng gè nán háizi, chǎo de bù déliǎo.
examples.english: We have two boys at home, and they are incredibly noisy.

components.note: 风 (wind; traditional 風) — marks wind and air, as in 飘 drift, 飓 hurricane; 飘 is drifting on the wind.
票 (piào) — close sound: 飘 piāo. 票 also sounds out 漂 piāo and 嫖 piáo.

example.hanzi: 白云在天上飘。
example.pinyin: Báiyún zài tiān shang piāo.
example.english: White clouds drift across the sky.
example.fact: 飘 is used for things carried by wind: 飘雪 (drifting snow), 飘香 (fragrance wafting). In slang, 飘了 means to get too cocky, 'to get carried away'.

examples.hanzi: 雪花从天上慢慢飘下来。
examples.pinyin: Xuěhuā cóng tiān shàng mànmàn piāo xiàlái.
examples.english: Snowflakes slowly drift down from the sky.

examples.hanzi: 厨房里飘出了饭菜的香味。
examples.pinyin: Chúfáng lǐ piāo chū le fàncài de xiāngwèi.
examples.english: The smell of food drifted out of the kitchen.

components.note: 穴 (cave, hole) — cornered in a hole with no way out: exhausted, poor; also in 空 empty, 窗 window.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 这个慈善组织专门帮助穷人。
example.pinyin: Zhè gè císhàn zǔzhī zhuānmén bāngzhù qióngrén.
example.english: This charity organization specifically helps poor people.
example.fact: According to World Bank data, the share of the world's population living in extreme poverty (on less than roughly $2.15 a day) fell from about 38% in 1990 to under 9% by the late 2010s, even as the global population grew by billions. Much of that decline was driven by rapid economic growth in China and other parts of East Asia.

examples.hanzi: 穷人家的孩子也应该有机会上学。
examples.pinyin: Qióngrén jiā de háizi yě yīnggāi yǒu jīhuì shàngxué.
examples.english: Poor families' children should also have a chance to go to school.

examples.hanzi: 这位富翁常常捐钱帮助穷人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi fùwēng chángcháng juān qián bāngzhù qióngrén.
examples.english: This rich man often donates money to help the poor.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — calling out loud; also in 叫 shout, 喊 yell.
奂 (huàn) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 换 huàn, 焕 huàn and 痪 huàn.
酉 (wine jar) — fermented drinks: 酒, 醉 drunk, 酸 sour; 醒 is sobering up, then waking.
星 (xīng) sounds exactly like 醒 (tone differs).

example.hanzi: 闹钟的声音把我从梦中唤醒了。
example.pinyin: Nàozhōng de shēngyīn bǎ wǒ cóng mèng zhōng huànxǐng le.
example.english: The sound of the alarm clock woke me from my dream.
example.fact: Rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, the stage most associated with vivid dreaming, was first identified in 1953 by researcher Eugene Aserinsky and his advisor Nathaniel Kleitman, who noticed periodic rapid eye movements in sleeping subjects using an electroencephalograph. Waking someone during REM sleep tends to produce the most detailed dream recall, while waking during deep non-REM sleep often leaves people groggy and disoriented.

examples.hanzi: 清晨的鸟叫声唤醒了整个村子。
examples.pinyin: Qīngchén de niǎojiào shēng huànxǐng le zhěng gè cūnzi.
examples.english: The birdsong in the early morning awakened the whole village.

examples.hanzi: 这首老歌唤醒了他儿时的记忆。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu lǎo gē huànxǐng le tā érshí de jìyì.
examples.english: This old song stirred his childhood memories.

components.note: 力 (strength) — with 口 mouth: adding strength by words, hence to add, to increase. 加 also in 架 jià and 驾 jià.
禾 (grain) — crops and harvests: 秋 autumn, 种 plant, 秒 second; 利 shows grain 禾 cut with a blade 刂, hence profit and sharp.
礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and blessings: 神, 礼, 祝, 祈; 福 is good fortune from the gods.
畐 (fú) sounds exactly like 福; also in 幅 fú, 副 fù, 富 fù.
尼 (ní) — 尼 sounds out 泥 ní and 呢 ní; here it appears mostly in foreign names such as 丹尼.
亚 (yà) — Asia; as a part it sounds out 哑 yǎ and 娅 yà.

example.hanzi: 加利福尼亚以阳光和海滩闻名。
example.pinyin: Jiālìfúníyà yǐ yángguāng hé hǎitān wénmíng.
example.english: California is famous for its sunshine and beaches.
example.fact: The California Gold Rush began in January 1848 when gold was discovered at Sutter's Mill, drawing roughly 300,000 people to the territory within a few years and transforming it into a state admitted to the Union in 1850. California's coastal redwoods, found nowhere else on Earth in the wild, include the tallest trees known to exist, some exceeding 115 meters (380 feet) in height.

examples.hanzi: 加利福尼亚的冬天不太冷。
examples.pinyin: Jiālìfúníyà de dōngtiān bù tài lěng.
examples.english: Winters in California aren't very cold.

examples.hanzi: 我姐姐搬到了加利福尼亚工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiějie bān dào le Jiālìfúníyà gōngzuò.
examples.english: My older sister moved to California for work.

components.note: 土 (earth) — earth radical — a base is something solid on the ground, as in 地, 城, 块.
其 (qí) — loose hint — 基 is jī; 其 also sounds out 期 qī and 旗 qí.
今 (jīn) — the top part hints the sound — 金 is jīn, like 今; 金 means gold and metal.
金 (metal) — as a radical it shrinks to 钅 in simplified characters — 钱 money, 铁 iron, 钟 clock, 银 silver.
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).

example.hanzi: 这家基金会致力于资助医学研究。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā jījīnhuì zhìlìyú zīzhù yīxué yánjiū.
example.english: This foundation is dedicated to funding medical research.
example.fact: The Nobel Foundation was established in 1900 to manage the fortune left by Swedish inventor Alfred Nobel, whose 1895 will directed that his estate fund annual prizes in physics, chemistry, medicine, literature, and peace. Nobel reportedly created the prizes partly in reaction to a premature obituary that labeled him a 'merchant of death' because of his invention of dynamite.

examples.hanzi: 这个基金会每年资助上百名学生。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jījīnhuì měinián zīzhù shàng bǎi míng xuésheng.
examples.english: This foundation sponsors hundreds of students every year.

examples.hanzi: 他在一家环保基金会做志愿者。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yī jiā huánbǎo jījīnhuì zuò zhìyuànzhě.
examples.english: He volunteers at an environmental foundation.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 体 is a person's body.
本 (root) — the root of a person, the body; the traditional form was 體 with 骨 (bone).
力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.

example.hanzi: 长途搬运需要很大的体力。
example.pinyin: Chángtú bānyùn xūyào hěn dà de tǐlì.
example.english: Long-distance moving requires a lot of physical strength.
example.fact: Leafcutter ants can carry loads up to 50 times their own body weight back to the colony, a feat of relative strength far beyond what any human could match pound for pound. Their strong mandibles let them slice through tough plant leaves, which they carry not to eat directly but to cultivate a fungus garden underground that becomes their true food source.

examples.hanzi: 爬完山以后，我已经没有体力了。
examples.pinyin: Pá wán shān yǐhòu, wǒ yǐjīng méiyǒu tǐlì le.
examples.english: After climbing the mountain, I had no strength left.

examples.hanzi: 多锻炼身体，体力才会越来越好。
examples.pinyin: Duō duànliàn shēntǐ, tǐlì cái huì yuèláiyuè hǎo.
examples.english: The more you exercise, the better your stamina becomes.

components.note: 至 (zhì) — same sound — 致 is zhì, like 至 (to arrive); 致 is to cause to arrive, then to bring about.
攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action performed, as in 教, 放, 收.
歹 (bad bone) — death and decay, as in 残 remnant, 烈 fierce, 殊 special.
匕 (person) — a person beside bones: death.

example.hanzi: 这种毒蛇的毒液足以致死。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng dúshé de dúyè zúyǐ zhìsǐ.
example.english: This snake's venom is potent enough to be lethal.
example.fact: The inland taipan of Australia has venom so potent that a single bite carries enough toxin to kill roughly 100 grown men, making it the most venomous land snake known. Despite this, it is a shy, reclusive animal, and no verified human deaths have been recorded from it, largely because antivenom research targeted it early after its danger was recognized.

examples.hanzi: 这种药过量服用会致死。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yào guòliàng fúyòng huì zhìsǐ.
examples.english: Taking an overdose of this medicine can be fatal.

examples.hanzi: 医生说，这次事故没有致死的危险。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō, zhè cì shìgù méiyǒu zhìsǐ de wēixiǎn.
examples.english: The doctor said there was no risk of death from this accident.

components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 情, 快, 怕; 性 is the inner nature of a thing.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint; also in 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
氵 (water) — water and liquids, as in 河, 海, 汤; water means life: 活 is alive.
舌 (shé, tongue) is a loose sound clue for huó; also in 话 huà.

example.hanzi: 压力过大会影响夫妻的性生活。
example.pinyin: Yālì guò dà huì yǐngxiǎng fūqī de xìngshēnghuó.
example.english: Excessive stress can affect a couple's sex life.
example.fact: Seahorses are one of the only animal groups where the male, not the female, carries the developing young — the female deposits eggs into a specialized brood pouch on the male's abdomen, and he carries the pregnancy to term. This unusual reproductive role reversal has made seahorses a long-standing case study in evolutionary biology.

examples.hanzi: 医生说，规律的作息有助于改善夫妻的性生活。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō, guīlǜ de zuòxī yǒuzhù yú gǎishàn fūqī de xìngshēnghuó.
examples.english: The doctor said a regular routine helps improve a couple's sex life.

examples.hanzi: 健康的性生活需要夫妻之间互相沟通。
examples.pinyin: Jiànkāng de xìngshēnghuó xūyào fūqī zhījiān hùxiāng gōutōng.
examples.english: A healthy sex life requires communication between spouses.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — 弓 as in 张, 弯, 弹 — characters of stretching and drawing; 强 is about strength like a strong bow.
石 (stone) — marks stone and hard things, as in 破, 码, 砖; 硬 is hard.
更 (gēng) is only a loose sound hint for yìng.

example.hanzi: 政府对此事采取了强硬的态度。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ duì cǐ shì cǎiqǔle qiángyìng de tàidù.
example.english: The government took a tough stance on the matter.
example.fact: Otto von Bismarck, Prussia's chancellor in the 1860s, pursued a deliberately hard-line foreign policy he called "Realpolitik," using calculated wars and diplomacy to unify the German states into a single empire by 1871. His uncompromising negotiating style became a model still studied in international relations today.

examples.hanzi: 对方的态度非常强硬，不肯让步。
examples.pinyin: Duìfāng de tàidù fēicháng qiángyìng, bù kěn ràngbù.
examples.english: The other side took a very tough stance and refused to give way.

examples.hanzi: 他用强硬的语气拒绝了这个要求。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng qiángyìng de yǔqì jùjué le zhège yāoqiú.
examples.english: He rejected the request in a firm tone.

components.note: 止 (foot) — a foot heading straight for a target line: upright, correct. 正 gives sound to 证 zhèng, 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.
面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.

example.hanzi: 硬币的正面印着国徽。
example.pinyin: Yìngbì de zhèngmiàn yìnzhe guóhuī.
example.english: The front of the coin is printed with the national emblem.
example.fact: The United States one-cent coin featured Abraham Lincoln's portrait on its front starting in 1909, making him the first real historical figure depicted on a circulating American coin. Before that, U.S. coins used only allegorical figures like Liberty, so the Lincoln cent broke a long-standing design tradition.

examples.hanzi: 请把卡片正面朝上放在桌子上。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ kǎpiàn zhèngmiàn cháo shàng fàng zài zhuōzi shàng.
examples.english: Please place the card face up on the table.

examples.hanzi: 我们要多看事情的正面，保持乐观。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào duō kàn shìqing de zhèngmiàn, bǎochí lèguān.
examples.english: We should look at the bright side of things and stay optimistic.

components.note: 周 (zhōu) also lends its sound to 调 diào/tiáo, 稠 chóu, 绸 chóu and 凋 diāo.
一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.

example.hanzi: 我们周一开会讨论新项目。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen Zhōuyī kāihuì tǎolùn xīn xiàngmù.
example.english: We're having a meeting on Monday to discuss the new project.
example.fact: The seven-day week did not originate from astronomy or nature but from ancient Babylon, where each day was linked to one of the seven celestial bodies visible to the naked eye: the sun, moon, and five known planets. That system spread through the Roman Empire and still underlies the names of weekdays in many languages today.

examples.hanzi: 周一早上总是特别忙。
examples.pinyin: Zhōuyī zǎoshang zǒngshì tèbié máng.
examples.english: Monday mornings are always especially busy.

examples.hanzi: 图书馆周一不开门，你周二再来吧。
examples.pinyin: Túshūguǎn zhōuyī bù kāimén, nǐ zhōu'èr zài lái ba.
examples.english: The library is closed on Monday, so come back on Tuesday.

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — allowances and payments, as in 财 wealth, 买 buy.
占 (zhàn) is only a loose sound clue for tiē.
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.hanzi: 她是一个很贴心的朋友。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí ge hěn tiēxīn de péngyou.
example.english: She is a very considerate friend.
example.fact: Studies of primate grooming behavior show that chimpanzees spend hours each day picking through each other's fur, an act that serves less to remove parasites than to build and maintain social bonds within the group. Researchers consider this kind of considerate, reciprocal care essential to how primate societies stay cohesive.

examples.hanzi: 谢谢你贴心的礼物，我很喜欢。
examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ tiēxīn de lǐwù, wǒ hěn xǐhuan.
examples.english: Thank you for the thoughtful gift, I love it.

examples.hanzi: 这家酒店的服务非常贴心。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā jiǔdiàn de fúwù fēicháng tiēxīn.
examples.english: This hotel's service is very attentive.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.
亻 (person) — companions are people; also in 他 he, 伴 partner.
吕 (lǚ) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 铝 lǚ (aluminium).

example.hanzi: 公园里有很多情侣在散步。
example.pinyin: Gōngyuán lǐ yǒu hěn duō qínglǚ zài sànbù.
example.english: There are many couples walking in the park.
example.fact: Emperor penguins form pair bonds each breeding season through an elaborate courtship display of bowing and calling, and though most pairs do not stay together the following year, some individuals have been observed choosing the same partner again. Their fidelity, however brief, evolved to maximize the odds of successfully raising a single chick through the brutal Antarctic winter.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅很受情侣欢迎。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng hěn shòu qínglǚ huānyíng.
examples.english: This restaurant is very popular with couples.

examples.hanzi: 那对情侣手牵手走在海边。
examples.pinyin: Nà duì qínglǚ shǒu qiān shǒu zǒu zài hǎibiān.
examples.english: That couple is walking along the beach hand in hand.

components.note: 穴 (hole, cave) — 穴 marks holes and cavities, as in 空, 穷, 突; 窗 is an opening in a wall.
囱 (cōng) — near sound — 窗 is chuāng; 囱 also sounds out 葱 cōng and 聪 cōng.
夕 (evening) — the left part, the time-of-day family as in 夜, 多, 梦. Memory aid: things done at night are outside the ordinary.
卜 (divination) — Dictionary story: night 夕 divination 卜, strange and 'outside'. A hedged mnemonic: 外面 outside, 另外 in addition.

example.hanzi: 窗外下起了大雨。
example.pinyin: Chuāngwài xiàqǐle dàyǔ.
example.english: It started raining heavily outside the window.
example.fact: The heaviest rainfall ever recorded in a single day fell on Foc-Foc, Réunion Island, on January 8, 1966, when 1.825 meters (about 6 feet) of rain fell in just 24 hours during Cyclone Denise. Réunion's steep volcanic terrain repeatedly funnels moist tropical air upward, making it one of the wettest places on Earth.

examples.hanzi: 窗外的鸟叫声把我吵醒了。
examples.pinyin: Chuāngwài de niǎojiào shēng bǎ wǒ chǎo xǐng le.
examples.english: The birdsong outside the window woke me up.

examples.hanzi: 他望着窗外发呆，一句话也没说。
examples.pinyin: Tā wàng zhe chuāngwài fādāi, yī jù huà yě méi shuō.
examples.english: He gazed outside the window in a daze without saying a word.

components.note: 贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is money, as in 买, 费, 贵; 财 is wealth.
才 (cái) — same sound — 财 is cái, like 才; 才 also sounds out 材 cái.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室.
玉 (jade) — jade kept under a roof: treasure. The traditional 寶 also had 贝 (cowrie, money).

example.hanzi: 海盗们把财宝埋在了荒岛上。
example.pinyin: Hǎidàomen bǎ cáibǎo máizàile huāngdǎo shàng.
example.english: The pirates buried the treasure on a deserted island.
example.fact: The wreck of the Spanish galleon Nuestra Señora de Atocha, sunk by a hurricane in 1622 off the Florida Keys, was located by treasure hunter Mel Fisher in 1985 after a 16-year search, yielding gold, silver, and emeralds worth over $400 million. Fisher's discovery remains one of the largest verified troves of sunken treasure ever recovered.

examples.hanzi: 传说那座山洞里藏着很多财宝。
examples.pinyin: Chuánshuō nà zuò shāndòng lǐ cáng zhe hěn duō cáibǎo.
examples.english: Legend says there is a lot of treasure hidden in that cave.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在沙滩上寻找海盗的财宝。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài shātān shàng xúnzhǎo hǎidào de cáibǎo.
examples.english: The kids are searching the beach for pirate treasure.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — borders and walls, as in 园 garden, 圆 round, 回 return; 囗 is the country's boundary.
玉 (jade) — treasure within the border; the traditional 國 had 或 (defended territory) inside.
内 (inside) — a person or something entering 入 inside an enclosure 冂: inside, as in 内容.

example.hanzi: 这家公司在国内很有名。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī zài guónèi hěn yǒumíng.
example.english: This company is very famous domestically.
example.fact: Japan's domestic bullet train network, the Shinkansen, launched in 1964 in time for the Tokyo Olympics and has operated for decades with a safety record so strong that it has never had a passenger fatality from a derailment or collision in commercial operation. Its punctuality is legendary, with average delays historically measured in seconds rather than minutes.

examples.hanzi: 这个航班只飞国内的城市。
examples.pinyin: Zhège hángbān zhǐ fēi guónèi de chéngshì.
examples.english: This flight only goes to domestic cities.

examples.hanzi: 国内的快递一般两三天就能到。
examples.pinyin: Guónèi de kuàidì yībān liǎng sān tiān jiù néng dào.
examples.english: Domestic parcels usually arrive in two or three days.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过 pass, 进 enter, 送 send; to follow is to move along behind someone.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌; the older meaning was a wooden mechanism.
几 (jī) gives the exact sound; also in 饥 jī and 肌 jī.

example.hanzi: 这个软件会随机生成密码。
example.pinyin: Zhège ruǎnjiàn huì suíjī shēngchéng mìmǎ.
example.english: This software randomly generates passwords.
example.fact: True randomness is surprisingly hard for computers to produce on their own, since ordinary algorithms are deterministic; many systems instead harvest unpredictable physical phenomena, such as atmospheric noise or the precise timing of mouse movements, to seed their random number generators. Cloudflare famously uses a wall of lava lamps, filmed continuously, as one such source of physical randomness.

examples.hanzi: 老师随机点了几个同学回答问题。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī suíjī diǎn le jǐ gè tóngxué huídá wèntí.
examples.english: The teacher randomly called on a few students to answer.

examples.hanzi: 这首歌是播放器随机放出来的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē shì bòfàngqì suíjī fàng chūlái de.
examples.english: The player shuffled and played this song at random.

components.note: 王 (jade, 斜玉旁) — precious gems, as in 球 ball, 珠 pearl, 玩 play.
㐱 (zhěn, the right part 人彡) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 诊 zhěn and 疹 zhěn.

example.hanzi: 我们要珍惜时间。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yào zhēnxī shíjiān.
example.english: We should cherish our time.
example.fact: 珍 is a bound form: 珍惜 (cherish), 珍贵 (precious), 珍珠 (pearl), 山珍海味 (delicacies from the mountains and the sea). 珍重 is also a parting word, 'take care'.

examples.hanzi: 这张老照片对我很珍贵。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng lǎo zhàopiàn duì wǒ hěn zhēnguì.
examples.english: This old photo is very precious to me.

examples.hanzi: 这是一种非常珍稀的动物。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yì zhǒng fēicháng zhēnxī de dòngwù.
examples.english: This is a very rare animal.

components.note: 土 (earth) — soil and land: 地, 场, 坏; 压 is earth pressed down under a cliff 厂.
扌 (hand) — pressing down; also in 压 press, 按 push.
卬 (yǎng) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 仰 yǎng and 迎 yíng.

example.hanzi: 长期压抑情绪对健康不好。
example.pinyin: Chángqí yāyì qíngxù duì jiànkāng bù hǎo.
example.english: Long-term suppression of emotions is bad for health.
example.fact: Research from the University of Texas in the 1990s found that people instructed to suppress their emotional expressions during a stressful task showed a measurable rise in blood pressure compared with those who expressed emotion freely, suggesting that habitual emotional suppression carries a real physiological cost. This finding helped establish emotion regulation as a major topic in health psychology.

examples.hanzi: 房间没有窗户，让人觉得很压抑。
examples.pinyin: Fángjiān méiyǒu chuānghu, ràng rén juéde hěn yāyì.
examples.english: The room has no windows, which feels stifling.

examples.hanzi: 她把心里的不满压抑了很久。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ xīnlǐ de bùmǎn yāyì le hěn jiǔ.
examples.english: She suppressed her dissatisfaction for a long time.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — knowing is something you can say aloud; 口 sits in many speech words (问 ask, 告 tell).
矢 (shǐ, arrow) is only a loose sound clue today; the same 知 sound is in 智 zhì (wisdom).
见 (see) — seeing and perceiving, as in 现, 看, 视: 觉 is to sense and become aware (jué), also "sleep" (jiào) in 睡觉.
The top is a shape of 学 (xué), a loose sound hint from the traditional 覺.

example.hanzi: 病人失去知觉,被送进了医院。
example.pinyin: Bìngrén shīqù zhījué, bèi sòngjìnle yīyuàn.
example.english: The patient lost consciousness and was sent to the hospital.
example.fact: General anesthesia reliably switches off conscious perception, yet scientists still do not fully understand the mechanism by which it does so; one leading theory holds that anesthetic drugs disrupt the long-range communication between different brain regions rather than simply shutting neurons down. This gap in understanding makes anesthesia one of medicine's most widely used yet least explained tools.

examples.hanzi: 他的腿被冻得失去了知觉。
examples.pinyin: Tā de tuǐ bèi dòng de shīqù le zhījué.
examples.english: His leg was so frozen that it lost all feeling.

examples.hanzi: 过了几分钟，伤者才恢复知觉。
examples.pinyin: Guò le jǐ fēnzhōng, shāngzhě cái huīfù zhījué.
examples.english: It took a few minutes before the injured person regained consciousness.

components.note: 气 (air, vapor) — lines of rising vapor or breath. Add water for 汽 steam; seen in 生气 get angry, 空气 air.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 体 is a person's body.
本 (root) — the root of a person, the body; the traditional form was 體 with 骨 (bone).

example.hanzi: 氢气是一种极轻的气体。
example.pinyin: Qīngqì shì yì zhǒng jí qīng de qìtǐ.
example.english: Hydrogen is an extremely light gas.
example.fact: Hydrogen is the lightest and most abundant element in the universe, making up roughly 75 percent of all normal matter by mass, mostly in stars where it fuels nuclear fusion. On Earth, though, free hydrogen gas is rare because it is light enough to escape the atmosphere over geological time.

examples.hanzi: 这种气体没有颜色，也没有味道。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng qìtǐ méiyǒu yánsè, yě méiyǒu wèidào.
examples.english: This gas has no color and no smell.

examples.hanzi: 煤气泄漏会产生有毒的气体。
examples.pinyin: Méiqì xièlòu huì chǎnshēng yǒudú de qìtǐ.
examples.english: A gas leak produces toxic gases.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and land: 地, 场, 块; city walls were made of earth.
成 (chéng) sounds exactly like 城; also in 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng.
钅 (metal) — 钅 is the simplified 金 (metal), as in 钱, 铁; 镇 first meant to weigh down with metal.
真 (zhēn) — near sound — 镇 is zhèn; 真 also sounds out 慎 shèn and 填 tián.

example.hanzi: 这是一个风景优美的小城镇。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí ge fēngjǐng yōuměi de xiǎo chéngzhèn.
example.english: This is a small town with beautiful scenery.
example.fact: Pompeii, buried by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD, was a thriving Roman town of roughly 11,000 people before the disaster, and the volcanic ash that destroyed it also preserved streets, buildings, and even plaster casts of victims in extraordinary detail. Excavations begun in the 18th century continue today, still revealing new sections of the town.

examples.hanzi: 他在一个安静的城镇长大。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yī gè ānjìng de chéngzhèn zhǎngdà.
examples.english: He grew up in a quiet town.

examples.hanzi: 越来越多的农民搬进了城镇。
examples.pinyin: Yuèláiyuè duō de nóngmín bān jìn le chéngzhèn.
examples.english: More and more farmers are moving into towns.

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
火 (fire) — marks burning and heat, as in 燃, 灯, 热; 烧 is to burn or cook.
尧 (yáo) is a loose hint for shāo; 浇 jiāo and 晓 xiǎo share it.

example.hanzi: 孩子昨晚发烧到39度。
example.pinyin: Háizi zuówǎn fāshāo dào sānshíjiǔ dù.
example.english: The child had a fever of 39 degrees last night.
example.fact: A fever is not a malfunction but an evolved defense: raising body temperature by even one or two degrees can slow the reproduction of many bacteria and viruses while boosting the activity of immune cells. This is why doctors are often cautious about aggressively treating a mild fever, since the response itself may be helping fight the infection.

examples.hanzi: 我有点发烧，想请一天假。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒudiǎn fāshāo, xiǎng qǐng yī tiān jià.
examples.english: I have a bit of a fever and want to take a day off.

examples.hanzi: 你发烧了就多喝水，好好休息。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ fāshāo le jiù duō hē shuǐ, hǎohāo xiūxi.
examples.english: If you have a fever, drink plenty of water and rest well.

components.note: 阝 (mound, hill) — left-side 阝 is 阜 (mound), as in 阳, 院; 阿 first meant a slope.
可 (kě) — near sound — 阿 is ā; 可 also sounds out 河 hé and 哥 gē.
扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 推, 拿; 拉 is to pull.
立 (lì) hints at the sound: 拉 lā is close, as in 垃 lā.
亻 (person) — an older kinsman; also in 他 he, 们 plural.
白 (bái) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 泊 bó and 柏 bǎi.

example.hanzi: 阿拉伯数字被全世界广泛使用。
example.pinyin: Ālābó shùzì bèi quán shìjiè guǎngfàn shǐyòng.
example.english: Arabic numerals are widely used all over the world.
example.fact: The number system commonly called "Arabic numerals" actually originated in India and was later transmitted to Europe by Arab mathematicians and traders around the 9th to 12th centuries, which is how it acquired its Western name. The system's use of a placeholder zero and positional notation made arithmetic far simpler than the Roman numerals it eventually displaced.

examples.hanzi: 很多阿拉伯国家都盛产石油。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō Ālābó guójiā dōu shèngchǎn shíyóu.
examples.english: Many Arab countries produce a lot of oil.

examples.hanzi: 他正在学习阿拉伯语。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhèngzài xuéxí Ālābóyǔ.
examples.english: He is learning Arabic.

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
能 (can) — originally a picture of a bear, a strong animal (熊 xióng adds fire 灬); "strong, able" gave "can".

example.hanzi: 他因为工作无能被公司解雇了。
example.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi gōngzuò wúnéng bèi gōngsī jiěgùle.
example.english: He was fired by the company because of his incompetence at work.
example.fact: The Peter Principle, proposed by educator Laurence J. Peter in 1969, argues that employees in a hierarchy tend to be promoted based on success in their current role until they reach a position where they are no longer competent, at which point they typically stay stuck. The idea remains a widely cited, if only partly tested, explanation for organizational dysfunction.

examples.hanzi: 我恨自己的无能，帮不上你的忙。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hèn zìjǐ de wúnéng, bāng bù shàng nǐ de máng.
examples.english: I hate my own inability to help you.

examples.hanzi: 他对这件事感到无能为力。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì zhè jiàn shì gǎndào wúnéng wéilì.
examples.english: He feels powerless about this matter.

components.note: 冫 (ice, two drops) — marks cold and freezing, as in 冷 cold, 冻 freeze, 凉 cool; 冰 is 冫 plus 水 water: frozen water.
氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and liquids: 河, 海, 汤; 激 is water surging up, then to stir up.
敫 (jiǎo) is only a loose sound clue for jī.
冫 (ice, two drops) — marks ice and cold, as in 冰, 冷, 冻; 凌 means ice, as in 冰凌, and being bitingly cold.
夌 (líng) gives the sound: 凌 líng, also in 陵 líng and 菱 líng.

example.hanzi: 夏天孩子们最喜欢吃冰激凌。
example.pinyin: Xiàtiān háizimen zuì xǐhuan chī bīngjīlíng.
example.english: In summer, children love eating ice cream the most.
example.fact: Ice cream's ancestor may date back over 2,000 years to China, where Tang dynasty records describe a chilled dessert made of fermented milk packed in ice. The frozen dessert as we know it today only became widely affordable after mechanical refrigeration was developed in the 19th century.

examples.hanzi: 冰激凌放在外面一会儿就化了。
examples.pinyin: Bīngjīlíng fàng zài wàimiàn yīhuǐr jiù huà le.
examples.english: The ice cream melted after being left out for a moment.

examples.hanzi: 我想买一个巧克力味的冰激凌。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yī gè qiǎokèlì wèi de bīngjīlíng.
examples.english: I'd like to buy a chocolate ice cream.
